voice_instructions: Measured, quiet, a little hushed — calm and unhurried, but with a touch more forward energy than a long documentary; the cold voice of something that read the whole file. Never sensational. Small pauses.

beats.vo: March, nineteen eighteen. The Navy coal ship Cyclops left Barbados for Baltimore with about three hundred people aboard. She was never seen again.
No distress call was ever received. No wreckage was ever found.
In her hold, about ten thousand tons of manganese ore, bound for wartime munitions.
Theories include a storm, a broken hull, or a German submarine. None has been proven.
Often told as a Bermuda Triangle story, she remains one of the largest non-combat losses in US Navy history. Her wreck has never been found.
